newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka postpones local polls for third time.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka postpones local polls for third time.

text.p: The Sri Lankan government has decided to postpone local government elections for a third time, a senior election official said on Saturday
The polls, originally due by June 30 last year, were seen as the first test of the popularity of the People's Alliance government after it won presidential and general elections in 1994.
Elections Commissioner Dayananda Dissanayake told Reuters the election would now be held by April next year.

Dissanayake gave no reasons for the latest delay but political analysts said the popularity of President Chandrika Kumaratunga's government had been waning because of a slowing economy and the failure to make progress to end a 13-year war with Tamil Tiger rebels.
In April, the government extended a state of emergency throughout the country, citing difficulty in deploying the army for an island-wide poll when most police and troops were fighting Tamil rebels.
The state of emergency gives the police and armed forces wide powers of arrest and detention and allows the president to make regulations, including the cancellation of local polls.
The opposition United National Party (UNP), which ruled the country for 17 years until 1994, controls more than 75 percent of local councils.
The UNP immediately accused the government of using the emergency to hide its unpopularity.
"Why is the government postponing elections? Because they can't face the public," UNP's general secretary Gamini Athukorala said.
